Lets talk about porting and getting the most out of your engine. When we talk about porting we are talking about trying to get the intake and exhaust manifolds to match the size of the transfer ports. Expanding them slightly will increase the flow and give you more power. The process is simple, and not very complicated, but requires patience and a steady hand.

Disclaimer: This was my first attempt. Read, read, read before you attempt on your own.

Album found here

Tools used: Dremel with high speed cutter. I couldnt find the exact one I used but it was close to this one. Mine had "teeth" all around the edge

Start by removing the exhaust and then remove the intake manifold. Remove the spark plug and then the four nuts holding the head in place. Remove the head and finally remove the cylinder. The cylinder might take a little force to remove. BE CAREFUL! Use a rubber mallet to gently tap the cylinder. The metal is soft so prying with a screwdriver or hammer could damage the cylinder. Also, be careful with the piston. I like putting a rag under the piston to keep it protected. Take this opportunity to clean all the parts you've removed. I used engine degreaser to get it nice and shiny.
